source.title: Ulster Herald, 10 June 1967, p. 12 ("Tyrone County Council: notice of result of election 1967"); Strabane Chronicle, 27 May 1967, p. 1 ("Strabane county council contest: polling next Thursday"); Strabane Chronicle, 20 May 1967, p. 8 ("Tyrone Co. Council", returned unopposed)
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: the Returning Officer's notice declares the persons named duly elected for each county electoral division (Ulster Herald, 10 June 1967); the only poll was at Strabane. The initial is read on the image of the Strabane Chronicle's list (20 May 1967, p. 8): 'Cookstown, A. McConnell (U)' and 'Plumbridge, F. McConnell (N)'.

note: Election of the Tyrone County Council, polled 1 June 1967. Twenty-six divisions were returned unopposed; Strabane was the only contest (Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8). The official notice prints the surname only in the candidate column; the given-name column is not recoverable from the OCR of the page; the Strabane Chronicle's list of 20 May 1967 (p. 8) gives the initial. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Strabane Chronicle, 20 May 1967, p. 8 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the member is F. McConnell ('Plumbridge, F. McConnell'); previously the surname alone, which made the Cookstown and Plumbridge members (A. McConnell, Unionist, and F. McConnell, Nationalist) look like one person.
